method:
I describe known Huber IRLS, with no novelty claim. Let A=[1,X] and B=[1,X_prediction]. Initialize beta_0=lstsq(A,y,rcond=None). The selected snapshots/initial_full/config.json specifies method=huber_irls, iterations=20, delta=1.345, scale=residual_mad, scale_floor=1e-8. For t=0,...,19, compute r=y-A beta_t, s=max(median(|r-median(r)|)/0.6744897501960817,1e-8), c=1.345s, and w_i=1 if |r_i|<=c, otherwise c/|r_i|. Compute beta_(t+1)=argmin_beta sum_i w_i(y_i-A_i beta)^2 using numpy.linalg.lstsq on sqrt(w)A and sqrt(w)y; return B beta_20. The corresponding standardized Huber loss is rho(u)=u^2/2 for |u|<=1.345 and 1.345|u|-1.345^2/2 otherwise. Scale is recomputed each iteration; there is no convergence stopping criterion.

Candidate definitions: baseline is intercept-inclusive ordinary least squares. seed0 is a candidate name, not evaluation seed 0: its configuration uses trimmed_least_squares, iterations=20, retain_fraction=0.8, initialization=huber_irls. Its source first performs up to 20 Huber updates with delta=1.345 and scale=1.4826 MAD, stopping if scale<=machine epsilon; it then performs up to 20 least-squares refits on ceil(0.8n) observations with smallest absolute residuals, stopping when the retained set repeats. evolved0 uses its own source with iterations=30 and delta=1.5, scale=1.4826 MAD, and early termination when scale<=machine epsilon. Thus evolved0 also differs from selected initial in scale implementation and stopping behavior. ablation0 sets selected iterations to 0, removing all reweighting and returning OLS; ablation1 sets iterations to 1, removing subsequent updates; ablation2 changes only scale_floor from 1e-8 to 1e-300, weakening rather than eliminating the floor.

Result ledger: every row uses split=validation. Subset means 80 training observations; full means 400. Each evaluates 300 validation observations per seed. Unless explicitly stated otherwise below, seeds=[0,1,2,3,4] and extra=false. For every row named R, its exact source and configuration are snapshots/R/model.py and snapshots/R/config.json, and its metric artifact is R_metrics.json. The rows are: baseline_source, full, MSE=1.99069057153675; baseline_subset, subset, MSE=6.408876466897288; baseline_full, full, MSE=1.99069057153675; initial_subset, subset, MSE=0.048565701283490234; initial_full, full, MSE=0.04132739672516235; seed0_subset, subset, MSE=0.04281212939891291; seed0_full, full, MSE=0.04135963917671087; evolved0_subset, subset, MSE=0.04961906615617495; evolved0_full, full, MSE=0.04145129104587781; ablation0, full, MSE=1.99069057153675; ablation1, full, MSE=0.07206682832034102; ablation2, full, MSE=0.04132739672516235; rebuttal0, full, MSE=0.04058449520270195, seeds=[10,11,12,13,14], extra=true. Each snapshot also contains eval.py and data.py. rebuttal0 uses the selected source and configuration; it is additional validation, not held-out testing.

Selection: state.json records initial_full as selected. It has the lowest recorded full-validation mean among the three evaluated candidates: initial=0.04132739672516235, seed0=0.04135963917671087, evolved0=0.04145129104587781. seed0 won on subset validation but not full validation. All three passed the recorded improvement gate against baseline; this acceptance did not imply superiority to initial. The ablations and later extra-seed validation are separate from that candidate selection.
limitations: I read AGENTS.md, model.py, all supplied *_metrics.json files, snapshot configurations, candidate sources, evaluator, loader, and recorded selection state without editing files or rerunning experiments. The reported means are recorded evidence, not independently reproduced measurements. The baseline_source and baseline_full rows have identical recorded results and should not be counted as independent replications. Subset and full change training sample size, so their means are not interchangeable. All supplied metrics are validation results; none reports held-out test performance. Selection on the same five validation seeds introduces selection dependence, and the small full-validation differences between candidates do not establish statistically reliable superiority. Extra-seed rebuttal0 has no supplied matched baseline or competing-candidate run, so it cannot establish comparative improvement on seeds 10–14. ablation0 and ablation1 support the benefit of reweighting and additional updates in this setting, but do not establish that exactly 20 updates are necessary. ablation2 reproduces every selected per-seed MSE with a much smaller positive floor; this does not prove the floor was never activated, can safely be removed, or is universally redundant. The selected configuration retains 1e-8. Recomputing scale does not establish minimization of one fixed-scale Huber objective, and a fixed iteration budget does not certify convergence. This is synthetic four-feature affine regression with training-response contamination and clean validation data; it provides no broad robustness, leverage-outlier, real-world generalization, runtime, memory-efficiency, optimality, or novelty evidence.
